mentions.name: Uruky
mentions.description: A private, paid, ad-free, personally customizable search engine. Signup requires no personal information (a randomly-generated account number is assigned), and a proof-of-work captcha grants 2 hours of free use. Users can pick among many search providers for defaults and per query, including Uruky Site Search, which is powered by the project's own index that is growing slowly with a focus on the indie/small web. Recently shipped features include an image search gallery mode, a calculator and conversion widget, and Tags and Scopes. After 12 months as a paying customer, users receive a copy of the source code (licensed BUSL, converting to AGPLv3 in 2 years).
mentions.problem: Offers a private, ad-free alternative to ad-driven search engines; the main ongoing challenge is discoverability and outreach, which is handled ethically without Big Tech or generative AI/LLMs.

mentions.description: This app is a simpler Kagi alternative: a privacy-focused, EU-based paid search engine. It launched image search, runs its own index and crawler, and has passed 150 monthly active accounts. Privacy features include URL rewrites, cash-by-mail payments, anonymous vouchers, and a 2-hour free trial unlocked via a local proof-of-work (Altcha) captcha; paying customers for 12 months can download the source code (BUSL converting to AGPLv3). Upcoming plans include voucher sales via ProxyStore with Monero/crypto payment and growing the indie/small-web-focused index.
mentions.problem: Its main challenge is discoverability and ethical outreach, so the team sponsors open source projects, maintainers, and indie/small-web/privacy websites.

mentions.name: Uruky
mentions.description: A paid web search engine positioned as a simpler and cheaper EU-based alternative to Kagi. Users can choose and sort among five search providers, search works without JavaScript, and results are personalizable through provider choice, domain boosting, and domain exclusion, with hashbangs (like "!g", "!d", or "!e") as a fallback. After 12 months as a paying customer, users receive a copy of the source code, and the team sponsors one privacy-focused project per month.

mentions.description: Uruky is an EU-based paid search engine positioned as a Kagi alternative. It aggregates results from multiple third-party search providers (with new provider deals added recently and an EUSP/STAAN API key still pending), has exited beta with paying customers, and offers short free trials arranged manually due to bot abuse. Search works without JavaScript, with the site serving HTML plus small JS enhancements, built on Deno, PostgreSQL, and Docker.
